source.title: Irish News, 6 June 1958, p. 1 ("County and rural council elections: Newtownabbey result"); Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1958, p. 7 ("Four contests in 23 divisions of Antrim County Council; Newtownabbey a new division"); Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1958, p. 5 ("Local elections: polling to-day")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: votes read from the result report: Robinson 3,615; Kerr 3,592; Telford 1,680; total poll 5,237 (34 per cent of 15,280). Two members were elected for the new division.

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received on 20 May 1958, withdrawals to 21 May, and polling on Thursday 5 June 1958 ('Polling to-day', Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1958, p. 5; 'results ... held ... yesterday', Irish News, 6 June 1958, p. 1). Four divisions were contested: Newtownabbey (two seats), Ballymena, Islandmagee and Randalstown. Party labels were printed only for the Newtownabbey candidates. New division created by the granting of urban status to the former Belfast rural district; two seats.
